title: Meals You Can't Miss
editorial: Singapore's most important food advice is structural: eat in hawker centres.

Chicken rice, laksa, char kway teow and chilli crab are the obvious starting points, but the real pleasure is moving between Chinese, Malay, Indian and Peranakan food without changing neighbourhoods, let alone countries.
Street vendors are not scattered everywhere because Singapore organised many of them into dedicated centres. This makes eating less visually chaotic and much easier to navigate.
Also carry tissues. We somehow spent days wondering why they were never available when we needed them.
